milestone: Collection — Theme-Scoped, Deduplicated Asset Registry (Phase 1: Foundation)
slice: Implements Phase 1 of the approved Collection plan, per the user's own request: 'i want to introduce concept of collection. the collection is created in builder along with theme. any asset am adding to any scene gets added into collection also. a scene always refer to the asset which is in collection. collection can have assets which are used in scenes and others which builder would want creator to have access for customization.' Clarified further: 'asset can be uploaded either to collection or scene. the final resting piece of an asset is collection. builder can delete from collection but not creator. when authoring an experience builder can connect with an asset available in collection or can upload a new one.' New Collection CRUD in projectModel.js (collectionAssets/findCollectionAsset/findCollectionAssetByRef/setCollectionAsset/registerCollectionAsset/retargetCollectionAssetRef/renameCollectionAsset/setCollectionAssetAvailability/collectionAssetUsageCount/deleteCollectionAsset), mirroring the already-proven Frame CRUD pattern 1:1 (a Frame is its own file, referenced by id, deleted by nulling every dangling reference in the same operation, 'AV-012') -- the one real difference is Collection needs no separate Scene-Layer reference scan the way Frame's _clearFrameReferences does, since layer.image has exactly one producer (the Experience mirror chain, _syncUniversalContent). A Collection entry is a derived, ref-indexed side table, NOT a new indirection layer -- experience.properties.imageSrc/graphicSrc and the mirrored layer.image field never change shape, still holding the exact same vihu-asset:/data: string every existing reader (AssetStore.resolve, ThemeRegistry.resolveAssetRef, externalizeSceneImage, the Draft Asset Architecture migration accessor) already expects; a Collection entry's own .ref field IS that string. Auto-registration hook wired into updateExperienceProperty (the one chokepoint every current and future producer -- the Decoration glyph-rasterization path, and Phase 2's still-to-be-built Image/Graphics picker upload -- already funnels through), so 'any asset added to a Scene also goes into Collection' with zero per-caller changes needed. A real correctness gap found via direct verification, not originally flagged, was closed in the same phase: Draft Asset Architecture's own lazy migration (AssetStore.migrateFieldsOnSave, called from _collectMigrationAccessors) can rewrite an Experience's imageSrc/graphicSrc from a legacy data: URI to a vihu-asset: reference for the exact same bytes, entirely independent of Collection -- without a fix, this would either orphan the existing Collection entry or spawn a wasteful duplicate; closed by teaching the migration accessor's own set callback to call the new retargetCollectionAssetRef(project, oldRef, newRef), which repoints an already-registered entry's .ref to follow the field rather than duplicating or orphaning. Verified via a new, comprehensive Playwright suite driving the real UI end to end: registerCollectionAsset fires correctly from the real Decoration glyph-rasterization click (exactly one entry, kind 'graphic', a real data: URI ref, defaulting to NOT available to Creator); reusing an existing ref on a second Experience (simulating Phase 2's future 'connect to an existing Collection asset' picker action) is a clean no-op, never a duplicate; a simulated vihu-asset: Image-picker upload registers its own distinct entry; the migration-retarget fix was proven end-to-end for real (this sandbox does have IndexedDB, so the real async AssetStore.migrateFieldsOnSave genuinely ran, confirmed via a real _persist() triggered by typing into the World Name field on Overview) -- the Collection entry correctly followed the field to its new vihu-asset: reference with zero duplication and zero orphaning; the retarget/delete functions were also exercised directly (a no-op retarget for an unregistered ref correctly returns null rather than fabricating an entry; Builder-only delete correctly nulls every dangling Experience reference, never fabricates a substitute, and correctly reports a false/no-op for an already-deleted id). Full regression: both goldenBuild.js suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) pass unchanged, confirming this phase touches neither compile/validate/publish pipeline; scene_dropdown_repro3.js (14/14, exercising Experience CRUD/graduation/attachment/Host Here dropdown heavily) passes unchanged, confirming the new updateExperienceProperty hook has zero effect on any pre-existing Experience behaviour. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; tools/world-builder/ (v1) and root Studio are completely untouched -- confined entirely to tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js and tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js. Phases 2 (Collection-aware picker for Experience Image/Graphics), 3 (Manage Collection screen + Builder-only delete UI), 4 (compile-time dedup in builder.js -- where 'reduces data load' is actually realized), 5 (Creator-facing availability metadata in the compiled package), and 6 (Creator-side 'From This World' browsing UI, per the user's own answered 'Both' to the one AskUserQuestion this plan raised) remain named, not-yet-started increments -- see /root/.claude/plans/witty-floating-thimble.md for the complete phased rollout.
